# skyler.tools

> Free, local-first trading tools: a position size calculator, a trade
> tracker and journal, and a compound calculator. Open source, no ads,
> no account — trades stay in the user's browser.

skyler.tools is a single-page web app for stock traders, built and used
daily by its author, Skyler Berry (@skylerber on X). It started in 2025
as a bare position-size calculator and grew into a spreadsheet
replacement across four iterations.

## What it does

- **Position sizing**: shares from account size, risk %, entry, and stop.
  Long and short. Purchased options size from delta and premium. Risk
  presets from 0.1% to 1% (viewable as fractions: ⅒ ⅛ ¼ ½ 1), a max-%
  account cap, and risk scenarios at half and double the chosen risk.
  Reverse solve: type the share count you actually bought and the
  implied risk % is derived backwards.
- **Trade tracking**: one-click logging from the calculator, trims and
  exits with R-multiple math, freeroll detection (stop at or beyond
  entry = worst case break-even), a next-action chip per position, and
  a timestamped journal with typed entries (thesis, update, review,
  lesson).
- **Compounding**: a 10-year table across yearly return rates, with
  contributions or withdrawals, milestone reads, and honest caveats
  (every figure is one constant hypothetical return).
- **Themes**: a reference of everyday one-liners for what listed companies
  do, grouped so you can browse a tape. Data lives in data/guide.json.

## Data and philosophy

Everything is stored in the browser (localStorage). There is no
skyler.tools backend or database. Optional cross-device sync writes to
a private GitHub gist the user owns; the token never touches a server.
JSON backup and CSV/TSV export are built in. Free, open source
(https://github.com/skylerberry/trade-tracker-v2), no ads, no account,
no subscription, no pay-to-win tier.

## Key terms

- **R (R-multiple)**: profit or loss measured against the amount risked
  at the stop. Risk $200 and make $200 = 1R.
- **Freeroll**: the stop has moved to or beyond entry, so the position
  can no longer lose money; the remainder runs risk-free.
- **Trim**: a partial sell that reduces open risk.
